result.summary:
Read core-directives.md, WF-02 Step 3b, docs/agents/design/REQ-026.md (all 10 ACs), decisions/0007-doors-time-in-t3h-reminder.md, then docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-026.md in full (branch feature/WF02-REQ-026, commit 9de5060). Cross-checked the spec's claims against the real implementation (apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts's buildEventCardContent/agendaLines, apps/bot/src/scheduler/reminderJobs.ts's composeReminder3h caption assembly, apps/bot/src/i18n/formatTimeInTimezone.ts) and, critically, against BACKEND-DEV's actually-committed test files (apps/bot/src/scheduler/reminderJobs.db.test.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/reminder24h.test.ts) rather than trusting the spec's own account of what those files do.

Checks performed:

1. AC7 exact-substring extraction (SOUND). reminderJobs.ts line 88 composes the doors caption line as exactly `${catalog.reminder3h.doorsLabel} ${formatDateTimeInTimezone(new Date(doorsItem.at), event.chapterTimezone, lang)}` -- label, one literal space, then the formatted time, nothing else on the line. event.ts line 862-863's agendaLines mapping calls the identical function with the identical three arguments (Date, event.chapterTimezone, lang) for the same AgendaItem. The spec's extraction method (split caption on \n, take the line starting with the English catalog.reminder3h.doorsLabel, strip that exact prefix plus one space, compare the remainder byte-for-byte === against cardDoorsLine.timeText) cannot introduce a formatting mismatch that isn't already present in the real strings, because the production code's own line format is exactly label+space+timeText -- the extraction mirrors the real composition rule rather than approximating it. Verified BACKEND-DEV's own committed AC7 case (reminderJobs.db.test.ts lines 420-433) only asserts `.toBe()` between cardDoorsLine.timeText and a separately-computed doorsText, plus a `.toContain()` on the caption -- it never extracts and exact-matches the caption's own doors line the way this spec's AC7 case does. This spec's AC7 case is a genuinely stronger, non-redundant proof, and its own-fixture claim (America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires vs BACKEND-DEV's Asia/Tashkent, different doors value/label, lang en vs ru) is accurate on inspection. PASS on this check.

2. AC8 'no leaked non-doors time' assertion granularity (SOUND AS AN ASSERTION, but the spec's claim that this is a coverage-gap closure is FALSE). formatDateTimeInTimezone (apps/bot/src/i18n/formatTimeInTimezone.ts) renders year+month+day+hour+minute via Intl.DateTimeFormat, so two distinct timestamps produce distinct full-string outputs with no realistic substring-collision risk (a bare '2026' cannot spuriously match because the assertion compares the WHOLE formatted string, not a fragment) -- the granularity is correct and the check is mechanically sound.

   However: the spec's AC8 section (docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-026.md lines ~362-370) and its 'Independence note' preamble (lines 29-32) both assert that this 'no other agenda item's own time leaks' check 'closes a gap' in BACKEND-DEV's own committed AC8 case, explicitly claiming BACKEND-DEV's case 'asserts .not.toContain(catalog.reminder3h.doorsLabel) only -- confirmed by reading the committed case directly, lines ~477 onward'. I read apps/bot/src/scheduler/reminderJobs.db.test.ts directly: line 477 is indeed the doorsLabel assertion, but the SAME test block (lines 479-487, the immediately following lines in the identical `it('AC8: ...')` block) already contains:
```
    if (networkingText !== startsText) {
      expect(message.caption).not.toContain(networkingText);
    }
    if (closingText !== startsText) {
      expect(message.caption).not.toContain(closingText);
    }
```
   This is the exact property (neither non-doors agenda item's own formatted time appears in the caption) that the test spec claims is missing from BACKEND-DEV's file and is introducing as new coverage. It is not missing -- BACKEND-DEV's own committed test already asserts it, immediately after the line TEST-DESIGNER's own citation stops at. TEST-DESIGNER's 'lines ~477 onward' citation appears to have been read only as far as line 477 and not the rest of the same test body.

   This is a factual misrepresentation of existing coverage, not a matter of interpretation -- the cited file and line range were named specifically and are checkable, and the claim is false. Per core-directives.md's 'Every producing step has a validating step' ('Re-derive under the conditions the property is actually about') and the Instruction Precedence chain's rule that a handoff's factual claims must be verified, not trusted, this is a validator-catchable defect in the artefact, independent of whether the underlying AC8 case is otherwise usable.

   Note: the AC8 case itself is NOT redundant on other grounds -- its use of 'workshop'/'afterparty' agenda-kind strings (vs BACKEND-DEV's 'networking'/'close') does genuinely test that findDoorsAgendaItem's kind==='doors' check is a real string-equality test against an independent vocabulary pair, which is a legitimate, distinct justification already stated correctly elsewhere in the same section. The case should very likely be KEPT -- but its narrative and the coverage table row for AC8 currently claim it closes a gap that does not exist, which must be corrected before this spec is accurate documentation for RELEASE-VALIDATOR or any future audit.

3. AC3 two-process construction (SOUND). Read apps/bot/src/scheduler/reminderJobs.ts's makeReminder24hJob: run(evaluationTime) sequentially `await`s sendLedgeredNotification per candidate inside a `for...of` loop (no fan-out). The spec's p1 harness calls `.run(evaluationTime).then(() => process.exit(0))` rather than awaiting inside try/finally -- since run() only resolves after every candidate's sendLedgeredNotification (and therefore sender.send) has already resolved, the .then() callback fires strictly after the one candidate's send has durably completed, matching REQ-025 AC1's established 'kill after first send resolves' discipline exactly, correctly extended from a bare sendLedgeredNotification call to a real job's run() entrypoint. Fresh Pool/drizzle per process, sidecar file hand-off, sequential p1-then-p2 execution requirement, and teardown list are all structurally identical in shape to REQ-025's already-gated AC1 harness (docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-025.md). PASS.

4. Forged-callback variants (SOUND, and non-redundant against each other). SECURITY-REVIEWER's own ad hoc scope (handoffs/WF02-REQ-026/step-02c-security-reviewer.json) ran 3 cases: no-registration attacker confirm, no-registration attacker decline, and own-registration attacker decline (the last specifically to rule out a 'silent redirect to caller's own registration' bug). This spec commits 2 of those 3 as a permanent file: no-registration-attacker+confirm, and own-registration-attacker+decline. These exercise genuinely different code (decideReconfirmOutcome/reconfirmRegistration vs decideWithdrawOutcome/withdrawRegistration), and the retained own-registration variant is paired with the decline handler specifically because that is the state-changing (seat-freeing) path where a silent-redirect bug would matter -- the dropped combination (no-registration-attacker+decline) tests the same ownership-check code (decideWithdrawOutcome, pre-existing REQ-022 code, unchanged by this diff) via a strictly weaker fixture than the retained own-registration+decline case already exercises, so its omission is a defensible scope narrowing, not a gap. Both retained cases check DB state unchanged (admission, reconfirmedAt) AND zero relevant audit rows for the victim's id, matching SECURITY-REVIEWER's own verified scope (which likewise checked DB state + audit rows, not notification-ledger counts). PASS.

5. Real grammY dispatch (CONFIRMED). The new reminder24h.forgery.test.ts is explicitly modeled on apps/bot/src/handlers/reminder24h.test.ts's own makeTestBot()/bot.handleUpdate(callbackUpdate(...)) pattern (confirmed those functions exist and are used at reminder24h.test.ts lines 79, 108, 206, 239, 267) -- no mocked grammY Context anywhere in either file.

6. No 'TODO' found anywhere in docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-026.md (grep -in TODO: zero matches). Every AC (1-10) plus the forged-callback property has at least one precise, mechanically-runnable case naming exact commands/fixtures/expected values -- this criterion alone would PASS.

VERDICT: FAIL, on check 2 alone (AC8's coverage-gap claim is false, verifiably, against the cited file and line range). This is a documentation-accuracy defect in a committed audit artefact, not a missing-coverage defect -- the AC still has a valid case -- but it must be corrected before this spec accurately represents what is genuinely new vs. already-committed, per Zero Manual Work's standing rule that a validator's job is to re-derive, not rubber-stamp, and per the explicit task instruction to verify this exact claim.

issues.location: docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-026.md, AC8 section (paragraph beginning 'A fresh event...') and its 3rd pass condition, plus the 'Independence note' preamble's AC8 bullet, plus the AC8 row of the Coverage table
issues.finding: Spec claims the 'neither non-doors item's own formatted time appears in the caption' assertion 'closes a gap' in BACKEND-DEV's committed AC8 case, citing 'reminderJobs.db.test.ts lines ~477 onward' as asserting only the doorsLabel absence. Independently read reminderJobs.db.test.ts lines 436-488: the same `it('AC8: ...')` block already contains, at lines 479-487, `if (networkingText !== startsText) { expect(message.caption).not.toContain(networkingText); }` and the identical guard for closingText -- i.e. BACKEND-DEV's own committed test ALREADY asserts absence of both non-doors items' own formatted times, immediately after the line the spec's own citation stops at.
issues.required_fix: TEST-DESIGNER must correct docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-026.md's AC8 section, the Independence note's AC8 bullet, and the Coverage table's AC8 row to state accurately that BACKEND-DEV's committed case already asserts this property (cite the real lines, 479-487, not just 477), and re-justify keeping this spec's own AC8 case solely on its legitimate, already-stated independent ground -- the deliberately different agenda-`kind` vocabulary ('workshop'/'afterparty' vs BACKEND-DEV's 'networking'/'close'), which is a genuine, non-redundant proof that findDoorsAgendaItem's kind==='doors' check is a real equality test. Do not remove the case -- it is still valid, non-redundant coverage on that narrower ground; only the false 'gap closure' framing needs correcting.

result.next_action: Rework TEST-DESIGNER — correct the AC8 mischaracterization identified above (docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-026.md), then resubmit to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 3b) for re-gate. All other checks (AC7 substring extraction, AC3 two-process construction, forged-callback variant coverage, real grammY dispatch throughout, no TODOs, per-AC case coverage and precision) PASS and do not need to be re-examined on the rework's expected single-hunk fix.
